result.summary:
ITEM 2 (FK-constraint fix): PASS, clean. Verified `foreign_key_constraint(:active_version_id, name: :artifact_activations_active_version_id_fkey)` (activation.ex:143-145) against the migration (priv/repo/migrations/20260831000001_create_artifact_activations.exs:60): name matches exactly. It lives in `Activation.changeset/2`, which both branches of `upsert_activation_pointer/8` call (activation.ex:406-414 insert branch, activation.ex:422-427 update branch) -- not a partial fix. Independently re-derived (not trusted) the ActivationHistory 'unreachable by construction' reasoning: `new_version_id` is the same `version_id` already FK-validated by `upsert_activation_pointer/8` earlier in the same `Ecto.Multi` (activation_step runs before history_step in `add_activation_steps/9`, confirmed by reading the pipe chain at activation.ex:338-350 vs 351-366); `previous_version_id` comes from an existing, already-validated row and is protected further by `on_delete: :restrict` on `active_version_id`'s own FK; `group_id` is inserted as the Multi's first step (`Multi.insert(:group, ...)`, activation.ex:253-254) before any `add_activation_steps/9` call, so a group-insert failure aborts the transaction before `insert_activation_history/12` is ever reached. Confirmed Postgres FKs here are IMMEDIATE (migration never opts into DEFERRABLE), so no ordering/race makes any of these three reachable after all. This item is correct and complete.

ITEM 1 (TEST-ONLY pause seam): FAILED -- narrow, implementation-level rework needed, not a design change. Reachability check: grepped every real call site of `activate_group(` in the tree; the only call sites anywhere are inside test/letflow/repository/activation_test.exs -- there is currently NO production/controller caller of activate_group at all (matches the design's own 'no route or controller added by this requirement' statement), so today there is zero live risk. But the seam's own moduledoc makes a specific, checkable safety claim that is FALSE: the `@typedoc` above `@type test_opts` says '`activate_group/4`'s public `@spec` above intentionally omits it so callers do not discover it by autocomplete' -- but the actual `@spec activate_group/5` (activation.ex:221-233) lists `test_opts()` directly as the type of its 5th argument, and `test_opts()` is a fully public (non-`@typep`) type whose definition (`[test_pause_after: pos_integer(), test_pause_fun: (-> any())]`) is visible to anyone reading or autocompleting against the module. This is exactly the class of documented-contract-vs-actual-behavior mismatch this same review chain already treated as blocking for the FK issue (@spec-vs-behavior mismatch, step-03b) -- here it's moduledoc-vs-code rather than spec-vs-runtime-behavior, but the same discipline applies: don't ship a safety claim that isn't true.

Structural safety is otherwise real: `maybe_add_test_pause_step(multi, index, index, pause_fun) when is_function(pause_fun, 0)` requires exact index equality plus a 0-arity function to fire; passing `opts \\ []` is a no-op; no arity-4-call-site regression exists. But structurally-hard-to-hit-by-accident is a weaker guarantee than the codebase's own established precedent for this exact class of problem. Checked test/letflow/engine_concurrency_test.exs (design's own REQ-055 precedent for concurrent-access testing): it needs NO production-code seam at all -- its properties (AC1's overlap-depth, AC2's exactly-one-success-one-conflict) are verified by racing real concurrent Task.async calls against real business logic and asserting on the outcome distribution, never by injecting a pause into the production code path. That precedent doesn't map directly onto REQ-203 AC2's requirement (proving an outside reader sees pre-commit state, which needs an actual pause point inside the transaction), so a seam of some kind is more justifiable here than TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR's summary implies -- but checked further: lib/letflow/design/req021-auth-plug-pipeline.md (OQ-5, lines ~254-286) is this codebase's own explicit, REVIEWER-reviewed precedent for 'we need a test-only substitution point but must not let it become an ad hoc reachable-in-production branch' -- and it explicitly rejects 'ELIXIR-DEV directly branching on Mix.env() inside AuthPipeline' in favor of a config-resolved indirection point (Application.get_env-selected implementation, defaulting to the real one in dev/prod, overridden only by config/test.exs). The current pause seam is a third, weaker shape than either of this codebase's own precedents: not a config-resolved indirection (req021's pattern) and not a no-seam race-based test (engine_concurrency's pattern) -- it's a public opts keyword accepted directly by production code, gated only by argument-matching, with a moduledoc that inaccurately claims it's hidden.

DECISION: requires ELIXIR-DEV rework, narrow (no CODE-DESIGNER involvement -- this doesn't need a new design, just closing a real gap in an existing implementation-level seam):
1. Add a compile-time kill switch so the pause step can never execute outside `MIX_ENV=test`, regardless of what opts a future caller supplies -- via `Application.compile_env(:letflow, :activation_test_hooks_enabled?, false)` read once into a module attribute, defaulting `false`, flipped to `true` only in `config/test.exs`. Gate `maybe_add_test_pause_step/4`'s functional clause on this compiled-in flag (an `if` on a module attribute, not a runtime `Mix.env()` call -- `Mix.env/0` is unavailable in a compiled release and this codebase's own req021 design already treats ad hoc `Mix.env()` branching as the pattern to avoid; `Application.compile_env/3` is this project's own established 'config-sourced, not hardcoded' discipline for exactly this situation, matching REQ-021's OQ-5 resolution). This makes the seam a genuine no-op in dev/prod builds, not merely one that's hard to trigger by accident.
2. Fix the moduledoc/typedoc's false claim: either (a) stop claiming `test_opts()` is omitted from the public `@spec` (since removing it from the `@spec` union entirely, in favor of a plain `keyword()` type for the 5th arg with `@type test_opts` marked `@typep`, would make the claim true), or (b) rewrite the claim to accurately describe the actual guarantee (structural argument-matching plus, after fix 1, compile-time exclusion in non-test builds) instead of an autocomplete-discoverability claim that the current code contradicts. Prefer (a) -- keep the detailed shape documented for readers of the module source (moved to a comment or `@typep`), but stop advertising the keyword shape in the public function's own `@spec` line, so a caller reading only the public contract via `h Letflow.Repository.Activation.activate_group/5` or editor autocomplete on the `@spec` genuinely does not see `test_pause_after`/`test_pause_fun`.
3. Do not restructure this into a full behaviour/adapter-swap module (that would be over-engineering relative to what a single pause point needs, and scope creep beyond this narrow gap) -- the config-flag-gated keyword approach is the minimum fix that (a) makes the moduledoc's safety claim true and (b) closes the residual 'could ever fire in prod' question definitively, without introducing new abstractions REQ-203 doesn't need.

No other part of this diff needs rework. The FK-constraint fix (item 2 above) is correct and does not need to be touched again.
